text.en: The self-designation *ainu* means 'person' ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--the-self-designation-ainu-means-person⟧. The language has three primary dialect divisions: Hokkaido, Sakhalin, and the Kurile Islands ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--the-three-primary-dialect-divisions-of-ainu-are⟧. Ainu has a relatively small phonemic inventory compared to the world's languages, and its syllable structure is not complex ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-has-a-relatively-small-phonemic-inventory-compared⟧. In complex sentences, Ainu exhibits predominantly dependent-marking patterns, as in relative clauses and most subordinate clauses ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--in-complex-sentences-ainu-exhibits-predominantly-dependent-marking⟧. The syntactic process of head movement is not essential in describing the grammatical structure of Ainu ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--the-syntactic-process-of-head-movement-is-not⟧.
text.ja: 自称*ainu*は「人」を意味する⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--the-self-designation-ainu-means-person⟧。アイヌ語の三つの大区分は北海道、樺太、千島の方言である⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--the-three-primary-dialect-divisions-of-ainu-are⟧。アイヌ語は世界の言語の中でも比較的音素の数が少なく、音節構造も複雑ではない⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-has-a-relatively-small-phonemic-inventory-compared⟧。複文においてアイヌ語は、関係節や大部分の従属節に見られるように、主に従属部標示のパターンを示す⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--in-complex-sentences-ainu-exhibits-predominantly-dependent-marking⟧。アイヌ語の文法構造を記述するにあたって、主要部移動のプロセスは本質的ではない⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--the-syntactic-process-of-head-movement-is-not⟧。

text.en: Ainu is a genetic isolate that differs strikingly from the languages of Northeast Asia, including the Altaic languages, Korean, Japanese, Nivkh, Yukaghir, and Chukchi-Kamchatkan ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--the-ainu-language-differs-strikingly-from-the-languages⟧, and is grammatically entirely dissimilar to Japanese, in contrast to many neighboring languages that share grammatical similarities with it ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--grammatically-ainu-can-be-described-as-entirely-dissimilar⟧. Typologically, Ainu is consistently described as agglutinating, polysynthetic, and head-marking ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-a-polysynthetic-agglutinating-predominantly-head-marking⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-agglutinating-polysynthetic-and-incorporating-language-2⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-exhibits-sv-aov-constituent-order-and-is⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-agglutinating-language⟧. It is also an incorporating language with SOV constituent order ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-agglutinating-polysynthetic-and-incorporating-language-2⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-exhibits-sv-aov-constituent-order-and-is⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-characterized-by-sov-basic-word-order⟧. Ainu is characterized by the predominance of postpositions, person marking on verbs and nouns, and a rich valency-changing system, with polysynthesis manifested by productive noun incorporation ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-characterized-by-sov-basic-word-order⟧. Unlike the Tungusic languages of Sakhalin, Hokkaido Ainu lacks subordinating non-finite verbal forms ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--unlike-the-tungusic-languages-of-sakhalin-hokkaido-ainu⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語は孤立した言語であり、いわゆるアルタイ諸語、朝鮮語、日本語、ニヴフ語、ユカギール語、チュクチ・カムチャツカ諸語を含む北東アジアの諸言語と著しく異なっている⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--the-ainu-language-differs-strikingly-from-the-languages⟧。また、周辺の諸言語が日本語と類似した文法構造を持つ中において、アイヌ語は文法的には日本語とまったく似ていない言語といえる⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--grammatically-ainu-can-be-described-as-entirely-dissimilar⟧。類型論的にアイヌ語は、膠着的・複統合的・主要部標示型の言語として一貫して記述されている⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-a-polysynthetic-agglutinating-predominantly-head-marking⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-agglutinating-polysynthetic-and-incorporating-language-2⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-exhibits-sv-aov-constituent-order-and-is⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-agglutinating-language⟧。さらに抱合的であり、SOVの語順をもつ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-agglutinating-polysynthetic-and-incorporating-language-2⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-exhibits-sv-aov-constituent-order-and-is⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-characterized-by-sov-basic-word-order⟧。後置詞優勢、動詞および名詞における人称標示、豊かな結合価変化体系、そして生産的な抱合に示される複統合性を特徴とする⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-characterized-by-sov-basic-word-order⟧。樺太のツングース系諸言語とは異なり、北海道アイヌ語には従属的な非定形動詞形式が存在しない⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--unlike-the-tungusic-languages-of-sakhalin-hokkaido-ainu⟧。

text.en: Ainu belongs typologically to the predominantly head-marking language type, a characterisation asserted by multiple scholars ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--head-marking-typology⟧, and is head-marking both at the clause level and at the phrase level ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-head-marking-both-at-the-clause⟧. Most key grammatical features in Ainu are either directly or indirectly related to head-marking ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--most-key-grammatical-features-in-ainu-are-either⟧. Ainu is predominantly head-marking at the clause and noun phrase levels and partially at the sentence level, distinguishing it from the predominantly dependent-marking languages of Northeast Asia ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-predominantly-head-marking-at-the-clause⟧. The possible arguments of a verb are marked with personal affixes on the verb, which obligatorily marks arguments on the predicate as the clausal head ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--in-ainu-the-possible-arguments-subject-and-object⟧. Ainu is predominantly head-marking and prefixing ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-predominantly-head-marking-and-prefixing⟧. Nouns and personal pronouns lack case inflection ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-polysynthetic-agglutinating-and-predominantly-head-marking⟧, and Ainu has no verbal inflections ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-has-no-verbal-inflections⟧. Some adverbial clauses are head-marked, in that a conjunctive element can follow sentence-final intonation and be uttered with the following sentence or verb phrase ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--some-adverbial-clauses-are-head-marked-in-that⟧. In evidential noun complement clauses, Bugaeva proposes that the complementizer markers belong to the main clause while leaving the subordinate clause intact, exhibiting a head-marking pattern ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--in-evidential-noun-complement-clauses-the-complementizer-markers⟧. In complex sentences, however, Ainu exhibits predominantly dependent-marking patterns in relative clauses and most subordinate clauses ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--in-complex-sentences-ainu-exhibits-predominantly-dependent-marking⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語は類型論的に主として主要部標示型の言語に分類され、この特徴づけは複数の研究者によって主張されている⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--head-marking-typology⟧。節レベルと句レベルの双方において主要部標示言語である⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-head-marking-both-at-the-clause⟧。アイヌ語における主要な特徴の多くは、直接的または間接的に主要部標示と関連している⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--most-key-grammatical-features-in-ainu-are-either⟧。アイヌ語は節レベルおよび名詞句レベルで主に主要部標示であり、文レベルでも部分的に主要部標示であって、主に従属部標示である北東アジアの諸言語とは異なっている⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-predominantly-head-marking-at-the-clause⟧。動詞の可能な項は動詞の人称接辞によって標示され、節の主要部である述語上に義務的に項が標示される⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--in-ainu-the-possible-arguments-subject-and-object⟧。アイヌ語は主に主要部標示であり、接頭辞を用いる⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-predominantly-head-marking-and-prefixing⟧。名詞や人称代名詞は格変化せず⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-polysynthetic-agglutinating-and-predominantly-head-marking⟧、動詞の屈折も存在しない⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-has-no-verbal-inflections⟧。一部の副詞節は主要部標示であり、接続要素が文末イントネーションの後に現れて後続の文または動詞句とともに発話されることがある⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--some-adverbial-clauses-are-head-marked-in-that⟧。証拠性の名詞補文節において、Bugaevaは補文標識が主節に属し従属節は無傷のまま残されるという主要部標示型のパターンを示すと提案している⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--in-evidential-noun-complement-clauses-the-complementizer-markers⟧。ただし複文においては、関係節や大部分の従属節に見られるように、主に従属部標示のパターンを示す⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--in-complex-sentences-ainu-exhibits-predominantly-dependent-marking⟧。

text.en: Ainu is consistently described as a polysynthetic and incorporating language ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-agglutinating-polysynthetic-and-incorporating-language⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-a-polysynthetic-and-incorporating-language⟧. Ainu exhibits polysynthesis, wherein directional/applicative, reciprocal, and reflexive voice markers, as well as adverbs and nouns when semantically required, attach to the verb stem ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-exhibits-polysynthesis-wherein-directional-applicative-reciprocal-and⟧. Polysynthetic characteristics are more prominent in Classical Ainu than in the colloquial dialects ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--classical-ainu-polysynthetic-prominence⟧. Because Ainu is polysynthetic, many Ainu loanwords in Eastern Old Japanese are compounds or complex morphological derivations ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--because-ainu-is-polysynthetic-many-ainu-loanwords-in⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語は膠着型・複統合的・抱合型の言語として一貫して記述されている⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-agglutinating-polysynthetic-and-incorporating-language⟧⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-a-polysynthetic-and-incorporating-language⟧。アイヌ語には、指相・互相・再帰相の標識のほか、意義上必要のある場合には副詞や名詞の類までも動詞の語幹に結びついてくる複統合性が存在する⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-exhibits-polysynthesis-wherein-directional-applicative-reciprocal-and⟧。複統合的な性質は口語方言よりも古典アイヌ語においてより顕著に見られる⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--classical-ainu-polysynthetic-prominence⟧。アイヌ語は複統合的言語であるため、東国上代日本語における多くのアイヌ語借用語はアイヌ語内部での複合語や複雑な形態論的派生語である⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--because-ainu-is-polysynthetic-many-ainu-loanwords-in⟧。

text.en: Ainu is an SOV language ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-sov-language⟧. The prevalent occurrence of prefixes in Ainu is an exceptional characteristic for an otherwise head-final SOV language ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-exhibits-a-prevalent-occurrence-of-prefixes-which⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語はSOV型の言語である⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-is-an-sov-language⟧。アイヌ語には接頭辞の頻繁な生起が見られ、これは典型的なSOV言語としては異例の特徴である⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-exhibits-a-prevalent-occurrence-of-prefixes-which⟧。

text.en: Ainu displays a mixed, but basically tripartite, alignment system ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-displays-a-mixed-but-basically-tripartite-alignment⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語は混合的であるが基本的には三分子配列のアライメントをもつ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-displays-a-mixed-but-basically-tripartite-alignment⟧。

text.en: Ainu extensively uses prefixation, a typological feature uncommon in the languages of the North Pacific Rim ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-extensively-uses-prefixation-a-typological-feature-uncommon⟧, and employs more prefixation than suffixation ⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-employs-more-prefixation-than-suffixation⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語は接頭辞を広汎に用いるが、これは北太平洋沿岸地域の言語では極めて珍しい類型論的特徴である⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-extensively-uses-prefixation-a-typological-feature-uncommon⟧。また、アイヌ語は接尾辞化よりも接頭辞化を多く用いる⟦claim:sources/typological-profile--ainu-employs-more-prefixation-than-suffixation⟧。
